title: The Questions Kept On Shaping
style: Urgent chamber punk anthem, brisk straight-ahead punk-rock pulse with driving kick and snare, distorted power-chord guitar, bowed cello doubling the bass movement, clipped violin and viola counterlines, and sharp ensemble stabs. Start with a tense string ostinato and close, determined lead vocal; bring in the full band for compact narrative verses, then open into a shouted, melodic gang-backed chorus. Use a brief stripped-down strings-and-voice bridge before the final chorus. Raw live-room energy, clear vocal up front, punchy drums, gritty guitars, tightly arranged chamber strings.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
In Sweden, first grade, I could count ahead
While the room learned numbers, I was turning pages
Back in Colombia, school days shifted course
Then eighth grade came, and the contest doors

[Pre-Chorus]
Nineteen eighty-six, a place among the twelve
Second-tier score, but I had more to tell
Next year, youngest finalist in the room
Best ninth-grader, chasing what came soon

[Chorus]
One more round, one more road to take
From a classroom desk to the world stage
Every hard problem left a mark on me
The numbers opened doors I couldn’t see

[Verse 2]
They called me in to train for bigger trials
I missed the cut, but stayed a little while
Kids from other cities shared what life could mean
While violence made its way across the screen

At fifteen, Australia, the team was set
Bronze in my hand, though day two left me blank
Then Cuba, silver, school bells closing in
Senior retreat, exams, and travel plans

[Chorus]
One more round, one more road to take
From a classroom desk to the world stage
Every hard problem left a mark on me
The numbers opened doors I couldn’t see

[Verse 3]
Top of the country, West Germany bound
Months before the wall came tumbling down
Graduation passed; I held university back
English lessons, computer skills, one last track

China came, another bronze to bring back home
Two points from silver, still I’d crossed the globe
Electronics, mathematics, proofs that wouldn’t bend
New foundations where quick instincts had to end

[Bridge]
Then I taught the minds that followed after me
Kept the national contest moving, year by year
In 2013, the world came to Colombia
And all those years of questions gathered here

[Final Chorus]
One more round, one more road to take
From a classroom desk to the world stage
Every hard problem left a mark on me
The numbers opened doors I couldn’t see
One more round, and the years still ring
From the youngest finalist to the ones I’d teach
Not just medals, not a finish line
The questions kept on shaping my life

[Outro]
The questions kept on shaping my life
